EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows strong aliphatic C–H stretches at 2879, 2908, and 2964 cm⁻¹, and CH2/CH3 bending near 1450–1466 cm⁻¹, consistent with a saturated hydrocarbon framework (GFQ-003). A prominent band at ~835 cm⁻¹ and another at ~960 cm⁻¹ are characteristic of cyclohexane-type ring modes (ring breathing and skeletal vibrations), favoring a cyclohexanol derivative over linear alcohols. Polyfunctional candidates (e.g., acetals/polyols) would typically show stronger C–O stretches around 1050–1150 cm⁻¹, which are absent, and the diazo candidate would require a ~2100 cm⁻¹ N≡N band, also absent. The methyl-substituted cyclohexanol (candidate 9) best matches the observed CH3 features (2964 cm⁻¹) together with the ring-mode pattern.
